title: Ward heritage district and heritage designations
subtitle: Royal Road rezoning against staff advice, Imperial Road hotel, and opposition to provincial Bills 5 and 17.
overview: Council approved the study for a new heritage conservation district in the west part of the Ward and named it The Ward Heritage Conservation District {{vote:m17}}. Staff will now draft a plan and guidelines, expected in about a year, with a statutory public meeting before council decides on the final plan. Council also approved a designation by-law for 72 Gordon Street after an owner objection {{vote:m10}}, and deferred the proposed designation of 5 Queen Street so staff can keep working with the owner {{vote:m16}}.

On planning applications, council approved a rezoning for a six-storey hotel at 725 Imperial Road North {{vote:m11}}. It also approved an official plan and zoning change at 81 Royal Road for a commercial industrial supply outlet, even though staff recommended refusal because the land is designated employment land {{vote:m15}}.

Council opposed provisions in provincial Bills 5 and 17 that it said would weaken environmental protections or override municipal planning authority, and will send the resolution to the Premier, ministers and AMO {{vote:m18}}. In closed session, council received information and gave direction to staff on a memorandum of agreement with CUPE Locals 241 and 973.

decisions.item: Ward West Heritage Conservation District Study
decisions.detail: Council approved the study's recommendations, named the area The Ward Heritage Conservation District, and directed staff to prepare a plan and guidelines.

decisions.item: 81 Royal Road official plan and zoning amendments
decisions.detail: Council approved the changes to allow a commercial industrial supply outlet on part of the site, after defeating the staff-recommended refusal.
Council approved a rezoning to permit a six-storey hotel beside an existing four-storey hotel.
Council received the owner's objection and approved the designation by-law for the property {{vote:m10}}.
Council deferred the notice of intention to designate to allow continued consultation with the property owner.
Council opposed provisions in the two provincial bills, endorsed the city's submissions on Bill 5, and will forward the resolution to the province and AMO.

debate: On 81 Royal Road, staff said the provincial definition of employment land now excludes retail and commercial uses, so the outlet did not fit industrial land. The applicant's team said most of the tenant's sales are to businesses and trades, and argued the use supports nearby employers.

On the same item, the mayor called the decision an 'elbows up' moment and said it was about whether the city is open for business. Staff said suitable commercial land was available elsewhere in the city. The parking rate staff proposed was lower than the applicant's request, but staff said more spaces could be built.

A delegate opposed the 5 Queen Street designation on the grounds of short notice, insurance difficulty for designated homes, and no incentives such as tax relief offered by other municipalities. Staff said they are compiling a list of insurers and supported a deferral. Tax relief programs are tied to later heritage district work.

On the Ward district, one councillor said renovation permits and approvals could burden owners of affordable homes and pointed to the earlier delegate's concerns. Others called these concerns largely myth, saying most work does not need a heritage permit. Staff said the guidelines would be flexible and would not delay current developments.

Delegates and councillors supporting the Bill 5 and 17 resolution cited Indigenous treaty rights, loss of environmental protections and municipal planning authority, and possible legal costs. The mayor said some Bill 17 provisions have merit, which is why the motion refers to provisions rather than the whole bill.
